plan.title: Whole-blood case/control cohort: consensus subgroup discovery beyond diagnosis
plan.analytical_narrative: The research question asks whether the 120 whole-blood samples (60 case, 60 control, single batch, Salmon gene-level counts, 12000 genes) fall into subgroups beyond the case/control label, how many, and how stable they are. This is a sample-clustering question, not a differential-expression question, so the plan follows the Inflexa-grounded clustering procedure rather than inventing an ad hoc approach. Track 1 establishes the count matrix's structure and removes low-information genes so that clustering runs on a defensible feature set: (T1S1) blind variance-stabilizing transform + PCA + sample-distance heatmap to see what already separates the 120 samples and to catch any single dominant outlier or artefact before subgroup discovery begins; (T1S2) a minimal filterByExpr low-count filter (edgeR, threshold 10 counts in >=60 samples, the smaller group size) so genes with no real signal do not add clustering noise. Track 2 is the central analysis: (T2S1) ConsensusClusterPlus resampling-based consensus clustering on the top 2000 most-variable genes from the VST matrix (item subsample 80%, 1000 reps, 1-Pearson-correlation distance with average linkage as stated in the grounded procedure), sweeping k=2 to 8 and selecting k from the consensus CDF delta-area and the proportion of ambiguous clustering (PAC), per the knowledge-service rule that delta-area alone can point to structure in noise. (T2S2) cross-tabulates the chosen clusters against case/control status, library size, and any other metadata columns available, because a subgroup that is really a library-depth or a case/control proxy is not a novel finding, and per rule R-0142 this check is mandatory before any cluster claim. (T2S3) supplies immune-cell composition (MCP-counter, on log2-CPM of the filtered counts) as a biologically interpretable covariate table beside the clusters, since whole blood composition (neutrophil/lymphocyte shifts) is the most common driver of blood transcriptome subgroups and the clusters must be checked against it rather than presented as intrinsic biology; this mirrors the pattern seen in comparable published whole-blood endotype discovery (e.g. PMID 41399015, four transcriptional clusters characterized partly by distinct immune-cell deconvolution profiles). (T2S4) runs a descriptive PCA-loadings summary of the genes driving the top components as the explicitly-flagged stand-in for NMF metagene discovery (NMF is absent from the environment; the knowledge service directs PCA loadings as the descriptive substitute, with the caveat that a PC mixes positive and negative weights and is not a metagene). Track 3 asks what distinguishes the discovered subgroups biologically: (T3S1) over-representation enrichment (clusterProfiler, MSigDB Hallmark, universe = tested genes, size window 15-500) of the marker genes for each subgroup (from a one-vs-rest limma comparison inside T3S1, since n=120 population-scale samples means limma-voom rather than a count model is the grounded choice for any group comparison here) against Hallmark, with WikiPathways human as a stated second collection from the reference store. Track 4 is the final report, which states explicitly per the knowledge service's clustering-report rule: the input transform, genes kept, distance/linkage, resampling count, the k evidence (CDF delta-area + PAC), the item- and cluster-consensus of each sample, the confounder table, and the caution that consensus clustering finds structure even in unstructured data, so any subgroup is reported as a hypothesis needing independent or external-cohort confirmation, not a settled subtype.
